description:
Every fact that the packaged profile and the adopter configuration reference restate is derived from its authority rather than kept in agreement by hand.

## Background

Three facts in this repository exist as two copies each, held correct by an assertion or by nothing at all.

The packaged profile embeds its whole directory into the binary at compile time, so an asset an adopter receives must live inside that directory. This repository also consumes the same files live at their working paths. The result is sixty-one asset pairs and one region pair, each carried twice in the tree. A test asserts every pair byte-identical, executable mode included, so drift fails the suite rather than shipping. Both copies are still hand-maintained, and keeping them equal is a step a contributor must remember on every edit. That test also walks one direction only: it checks each declared asset against the live file it mirrors and never checks that a live file belonging in the package was declared, so a newly added consumer is absent from every adopter install without anything reporting it.

The planning-bracket template declaration has no such guard. It is embedded inline in the profile manifest rather than shipped as an asset, so the byte-equality contract that covers the asset pairs does not reach it. The two declarations match on structure — roles, types, gates, document paths, labels, edges, and transforms — and already differ in three description strings, so the copies have drifted unreported.

The adopter configuration reference and the copyable example configuration restate the managed, permanent, and issue-scoped area lists in prose. Their authority is the shipped documentation-policy constant, and the initialization scaffold already renders that constant as the table a fresh repository receives. The reference cites the constant by name, which orients a reader, but nothing binds the values, and the example configuration carries a hand-chosen subset of the same entries. These lists went stale during earlier work and blocked two reviews before they were repaired.

Deriving the packaged asset tree also moves its live sources into the binary's build inputs. The inventory that tells a contributor their installed binary is stale is a positive list of paths, so unless it grows with the derivation, editing a live consumer changes the binary while the staleness report stays silent.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The adopter configuration reference and the copyable example configuration obtain the managed, permanent, and issue-scoped area lists from the shipped documentation-policy constant, and neither document retains a hand-maintained second copy of any of those lists.
- [hard] REQ-02: A change to either the repository planning-bracket template declaration or its packaged counterpart, without the corresponding change to the other, fails the test suite. The guard compares the two parsed declarations rather than a hand-written expectation of their contents.
- [hard] REQ-03: The packaged live-asset tree is derived from the repository files it mirrors rather than carried as a second checked-in copy, and editing a live file alone cannot leave the packaged copy stale.
- [hard] REQ-04: A build from unchanged sources and unchanged explicit environment stays byte-for-byte reproducible, and the derivation is ordered so that the embedded package always reads a fully populated tree.
- [hard] REQ-05: A repository file under a declared packaged root that is neither declared as a packaged asset nor declared as an exclusion fails the test suite, so a new live consumer cannot be omitted from the package unnoticed.
- [hard] REQ-06: Editing a live consumer alone reports a binary installed before that edit as stale.

## Decisions

- D-1: The repository planning-bracket template declaration is generated from the packaged contribution, which is the authority; the repository copy is a rendered region whose freshness the test suite checks. Rejected: synchronizing the three description strings and guarding deep equality of two hand-edited copies, which leaves both hand-maintained; guarding structure alone and letting descriptions diverge, which leaves REQ-02 unmet by construction.
- D-2: The packaged live-asset inventory stays an explicit per-file declaration and gains a declared root-and-exclusion list that turns omission into a failure. Rejected: include and exclude globs expanded at build time, because a missed exclusion over-packages an adopter install, which is worse than the omission it prevents.
- D-3: Only the `[documentation]` table of the copyable example configuration becomes generated; the rest of that file stays hand-authored, and its present illustrative subset gives way to the shipped table a fresh repository actually receives. Rejected: replacing that whole file with the initialization scaffold, which would add and remove unrelated tables for reasons this work does not decide.
- D-4: The shipped policy reaches both documents through a repository-local generator that initializes a throwaway repository and reads the table the shipped code path wrote there, verified by a mechanical freshness check. Rejected: a new command that prints the shipped policy, which adds adopter-visible surface whose only consumer is this repository's documentation pipeline; a projection over a new engine item kind, which would need a source mode for a compiled constant that no declared kind has.

## Notes

REQ-03 changes a declared binary build input, so every downstream verdict rebuilds once it lands.

The ordering in REQ-04 is the load-bearing risk. The embedding macro reads the package directory at compile time; a derivation that runs after it produces a silently stale binary rather than an error, which is the one failure mode this change must not introduce.

Upholds `@/invariant/single-source-prose`.
title: Derived profile assets and projected policy documentation
